hook.situation: You ask a classmate about a presentation assignment before midterms, plan when to start studying, talk about exam period, and explain why grades or scholarships matter.
objectives: Talk about assignments, presentations, midterms, finals, semesters, grades, and study plans.
Use V아/어야 해요, V기로 했어요, V기 시작하다, N 동안, and V기 위해서 in school-life sentences.
Separate class obligations, personal decisions, study periods, and exam goals.
hook.whyItMatters: Education Korean is deadline-heavy. Learners need more than 학교 and 시험: they need to say what must be finished, what was decided, when exam period lasts, and why they are studying.

grammarNotes.title: V아/어야 해요 — school obligation
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when a class, teacher, professor, or exam creates something you have to do.
grammarNotes.formation: Make the 아/어 form and add 야 해요. 하다 verbs become 해야 해요, so 공부하다 becomes 공부해야 해요 and 발표하다 becomes 발표해야 해요.

examples.ko: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요.
examples.romanization: junggangosa jeone balpyo gwajereul kkeutnaeya haeyo.
examples.en: We have to finish the presentation assignment before the midterm.
I have to present in class tomorrow.
I have to study more before the final exam.
If I want to get a scholarship, I need good grades.

grammarNotes.title: V기로 했어요 — decided to V
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this for a study plan or class decision that has already been set.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -기로 했어요 to the verb stem: 끝내기로 했어요, 공부하기로 했어요, 질문하기로 했어요. Keep 했어요 because the decision was made before now.

examples.en: We decided to finish the assignment before the midterm.
I decided to study at the library starting today.
I decided to ask the professor.
I decided not to be absent this semester.

exceptions: 가기로 할 거예요 means 'I will decide to go,' not 'I decided to go.' For an already-set plan, use 했어요.

grammarNotes.title: V기 시작하다 — start doing
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when the study action begins: studying, preparing, reviewing, or attending.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -기 to the verb stem, then add 시작하다. 공부하다 becomes 공부하기 시작하다, 준비하다 becomes 준비하기 시작하다.

examples.en: I started exam study from today.
I started preparing from today.

examples.ko: 한국어를 배우기 시작한 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.romanization: hangugeoreul baeugi sijakan ji il nyeon dwaesseoyo.
examples.en: It has been one year since I started learning Korean.
When midterm period starts, the library gets crowded.

grammarNotes.title: N 동안 — for/during a study period
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 동안 for a stretch of time, such as a semester, exam period, vacation, or one hour.
grammarNotes.formation: Put the time noun before 동안 with no particle: 한 학기 동안, 시험 기간 동안, 방학 동안, 세 시간 동안.

examples.ko: 시험 기간 동안 도서관에서 공부할 거예요.
examples.romanization: siheom gigan dongan doseogwaneseo gongbuhal geoyeyo.
examples.en: During exam period, I will study at the library.
I reviewed every day during this semester.
I went to an academy during vacation.
I worked on the assignment for two hours.

exceptions: Use 에 for a point in time: 세 시에. Use 동안 for a stretch: 세 시간 동안.

grammarNotes.title: V/A(으)니까 — reason before a school request or plan
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when the reason supports what someone should do next.
grammarNotes.formation: Add -니까 after a vowel stem and -으니까 after a consonant stem. With 하다 adjectives, use 하니까.

examples.en: Grades are important, so we have to prepare.
The midterm is close, so I study at the library.
There are many assignments, so I am starting today.

examples.ko: 교수님께 질문해야 하니까 수업 후에 남을게요.
examples.romanization: gyosunimkke jilmunhaeya hanikka sueop hue nameulgeyo.
examples.en: I need to ask the professor, so I will stay after class.

grammarNotes.title: V기 위해서 — in order to
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this for deliberate school goals: passing, getting a scholarship, improving grades, or entering a program.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -기 위해서 to the verb stem: 합격하기 위해서, 장학금을 받기 위해서, 한국어를 잘하기 위해서.

examples.ko: 기말고사에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해 매일 공부해야 해요.
examples.romanization: gimalgosaeseo joeun seongjeogeul batgi wihae maeil gongbuhaeya haeyo.
examples.en: I have to study every day in order to get a good grade on the final exam.

examples.ko: 장학금을 받기 위해 좋은 성적이 필요해요.
examples.romanization: janghakgeumeul batgi wihae joeun seongjeogi piryohaeyo.
examples.en: Good grades are necessary in order to get a scholarship.
I asked the professor a question in order to change my major.
I go to an academy in order to get good at Korean.

exampleSentence.ko: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: We have to finish the presentation assignment before the midterm.
We decided to finish the assignment before the midterm.

exampleSentence.ko: 기말고사에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해 매일 공부해야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: I have to study every day in order to get a good grade on the final exam.
I reviewed every day during this semester.
I decided to ask the professor.
I have to present in class tomorrow.

exampleSentence.ko: 시험 기간 동안 도서관에서 공부할 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: During exam period, I will study at the library.
I decided to study at the library starting today.

exampleSentence.ko: 장학금을 받기 위해 좋은 성적이 필요해요.
exampleSentence.en: Good grades are necessary in order to get a scholarship.

exampleSentence.ko: 장학금을 받기 위해 좋은 성적이 필요해요.
exampleSentence.en: Good grades are necessary in order to get a scholarship.
I asked the professor a question in order to change my major.
I go to an academy in order to get good at Korean.

extendedDialogue.setting: Classmates plan around a presentation assignment and upcoming exams.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요?
lines.romanization: junggangosa jeone balpyo gwajereul kkeutnaeya haeyo?
lines.en: Do we have to finish the presentation assignment before the midterm?

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 네, 이번 학기 성적에 들어가니까 준비해야 해요.
lines.romanization: ne, ibeon hakgi seongjeoge deureoganikka junbihaeya haeyo.
lines.en: Yes, it counts toward this semester's grade, so we have to prepare.
lines.grammarNote: -니까 gives the reason for the obligation.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 그럼 오늘부터 도서관에서 공부하기 시작하기로 했어요.
lines.romanization: geureom oneulbuteo doseogwaneseo gongbuhagi sijakagiro haesseoyo.
lines.en: Then I decided to start studying at the library from today.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 기말고사에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해 시험 기간 동안 매일 공부해야 해요.
lines.romanization: gimalgosaeseo joeun seongjeogeul batgi wihae siheom gigan dongan maeil gongbuhaeya haeyo.
lines.en: In order to get a good grade on the final exam, we have to study every day during exam period.
lines.grammarNote: -기 위해 and 동안 explain purpose and duration.

readingText.title: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요
readingText.body: 민서는 이번 학기에 한국어 수업을 듣고 있어요. 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해서 친구와 일정을 정했어요. 발표가 성적에 들어가니까 오늘부터 준비하기 시작하기로 했어요. 시험 기간 동안은 도서관에서 매일 공부할 거예요. 기말고사에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해 복습도 하고, 모르는 것은 교수님께 질문하기로 했어요. 장학금을 받으려면 좋은 성적이 필요하니까 이번 학기에는 더 꾸준히 공부해야 해요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo is taking a Korean class this semester. Because the presentation assignment must be finished before the midterm, Minseo made a schedule with a friend. Since the presentation counts toward the grade, they decided to start preparing from today. During exam period, Minseo will study at the library every day. In order to pass the final, Minseo will review and ask the professor about things they do not know. Since good grades are needed for a scholarship, Minseo has to study more consistently this semester.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 언제까지 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요?
시험 기간 동안 어디에서 공부할 거예요?

culturalNote.title: Grades Shape The Schedule
culturalNote.body: Korean school conversations often connect assignments, exams, grades, and future goals. A student may talk about 과제 and 발표 first, then 중간고사 or 기말고사, then 성적, 장학금, or 전공. The natural language is practical: 끝내야 해요, 준비하기 시작했어요, 시험 기간 동안, 합격하기 위해.
culturalNote.tip: Use 선생님 for school or language teachers, and 교수님 for university professors.

중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝낼 리가 없어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence states a study decision?

inlineExercises.explanation: Put 동안 directly after the time span noun.

bullets: Core flow: finish assignments before midterms, start preparing, study during exam period, and study for final goals.
V아/어야 해요 expresses school obligations; V기로 했어요 reports study decisions.
N 동안 marks a study period, while V기 위해서 marks a deliberate academic purpose.
과제, 발표, 중간고사, 기말고사, 성적, 장학금, 전공, and 교수님 should appear in real school sentences, not as isolated labels.
